    def materialise_electrode(
    world: World,
    spec: ElectrodeSpec,
    *,
    centre_xy: tuple[float, float],
    name: str,
    bond_conductor_type: str = "bare_copper",
) -> None:
    """Create one resolved electrode spec in ``world``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        Target world.
    spec
        Resolved electrode spec (concrete values only).
    centre_xy
        Electrode reference point ``(x, y)`` in m (site position plus
        the spec's ``offset_xy_m``).
    name
        Electrode name; a foundation built from several primitives uses
        it for its anchor primitive.
    bond_conductor_type
        Conductor type of the internal bonds of a multi-primitive
        foundation.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``spec`` is not a rod, ring, strip or foundation electrode
        spec.
    ValueError
        If a rectangular foundation has a side that is not positive
        (after the draws of a distribution).
    """
    ex, ey = centre_xy
    if isinstance(spec, RodElectrodeSpec):
        create_electrode(
            world,
            "rod",
            name=name,
            position=(ex, ey, float(spec.depth_m)),
            length=float(spec.length_m),
            wire_radius=spec.wire_radius_m,
        )
        return
    if isinstance(spec, RingElectrodeSpec):
        create_electrode(
            world,
            "ring",
            name=name,
            center=(ex, ey, float(spec.depth_m)),
            radius=float(spec.radius_m),
            wire_radius=spec.wire_radius_m,
        )
        return
    if isinstance(spec, StripElectrodeSpec):
        length = float(spec.length_m)
        angle = math.radians(float(spec.orientation_deg))
        depth = float(spec.depth_m)
        sx = ex - 0.5 * length * math.cos(angle)
        sy = ey - 0.5 * length * math.sin(angle)
        tx = ex + 0.5 * length * math.cos(angle)
        ty = ey + 0.5 * length * math.sin(angle)
        create_electrode(
            world,
            "strip",
            name=name,
            start=(sx, sy, depth),
            end=(tx, ty, depth),
            wire_radius=spec.wire_radius_m,
        )
        return
    if isinstance(spec, FoundationElectrodeSpec):
        _materialise_foundation(
            world,
            spec,
            centre_xy=(ex, ey),
            name=name,
            bond_conductor_type=bond_conductor_type,
        )
        return
    raise TypeError(
        f"materialise_electrode: unknown electrode spec {type(spec).__name__}."
    )

    def materialise_junction(world: World, junction: PlannedJunction) -> str:
    """Create a PEN cable joint and return its node name.

    The joint is a leakage-free :class:`~groundfield.geometry.junction.Junction`
    at ``(x, y, depth_m)``: a node of the conductor network with
    Kirchhoff's current law and no soil contact. Up to 0.15.0 it was a
    5 cm driven rod, which leaked 3 to 7 % of a test current through the
    nominally isolated cable (review finding 10.38).

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        Target world.
    junction
        The planned joint: its name, plan position ``position_xy`` in m
        and depth ``depth_m`` in m.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The name of the created junction (``junction.name``).
    """
    create_junction(
        world,
        position=(junction.position_xy[0], junction.position_xy[1], junction.depth_m),
        name=junction.name,
    )
    return junction.name

With axis_z_m both ends are moved to that depth, with axis_offset_m both ends move by that distance along the normal of the plan direction (decision D9: service drops in a row), or along axis_offset_normal_xy when the plan gives one (the common normal of a row of drops that are not exactly parallel, audit W3R2B-01).

    point of the node (the site's anchor electrode, or the junction). With
    ``axis_z_m`` both ends are moved to that depth, with ``axis_offset_m``
    both ends move by that distance along the normal of the plan direction
    (decision D9: service drops in a row), or along
    ``axis_offset_normal_xy`` when the plan gives one (the common normal of
    a row of drops that are not exactly parallel, audit W3R2B-01).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a contact names an electrode that is not a horizontal wire
        (foundation, ring, strip) of the site the branch ends at (with
        ``foundation_wires``; without it, an electrode that is no strip,
        polyline or ring), or lies farther from that wire in plan (from the
        exact circle of a ring) than one minimum cable section
        (:func:`~groundfield.generators._pen_routing.min_section_length` of
        the branch's conductor: 1 cm for wire radii up to 7.3 mm; audit
        R4A-05); or if a branch with ``axis_offset_m`` has no horizontal
        extent.
    """
    start = nodes.get(branch.start, branch.start)
    end = nodes.get(branch.end, branch.end)
    if index is not None:
        start_node, end_node = index.get(start, start), index.get(end, end)
    else:
        start_node, end_node = start, end
    p = branch.conductor
    if (
        branch.axis_z_m is None
        and branch.start_contact is None
        and branch.end_contact is None
        and branch.axis_offset_m == 0.0
    ):
        return create_conductor(
            world,
            name=branch.name,
            start=start_node,
            end=end_node,
            conductor_type=p.conductor_type,
            wire_radius=p.wire_radius_m,
            cross_section=p.cross_section,
            discretize_segment_length=p.segment_length_m,
            coupling_to_soil=p.coupling_to_soil,
            inductance_model=p.inductance_model,
        )
    (sx, sy, sz), start = _branch_end(
        world,
        start_node,
        start,
        branch.start_contact,
        index,
        branch=branch,
        site=branch.start,
        foundation_wires=foundation_wires,
    )
    (ex, ey, ez), end = _branch_end(
        world,
        end_node,
        end,
        branch.end_contact,
        index,
        branch=branch,
        site=branch.end,
        foundation_wires=foundation_wires,
    )
    if branch.axis_z_m is not None:
        sz = ez = float(branch.axis_z_m)
    if branch.axis_offset_m != 0.0 and branch.axis_offset_normal_xy is not None:
        # a drop in a row that is not exactly parallel (audit W3R2B-01): both
        # ends along the row's common normal
        nx, ny = branch.axis_offset_normal_xy
        offset = float(branch.axis_offset_m)
        sx, sy = sx + offset * nx, sy + offset * ny
        ex, ey = ex + offset * nx, ey + offset * ny
    elif branch.axis_offset_m != 0.0:
        # a drop in a row (decision D9): both ends along the left normal of
        # the plan direction; the conductor stays attached to its nodes
        dx, dy = ex - sx, ey - sy
        length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        if length == 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"materialise_branch: branch {branch.name!r} has "
                f"axis_offset_m = {branch.axis_offset_m!r} but no horizontal "
                "extent (its ends coincide in plan), so the offset has no "
                "direction."
            )
        shift = float(branch.axis_offset_m) / length
        sx, sy = sx - dy * shift, sy + dx * shift
        ex, ey = ex - dy * shift, ey + dx * shift
    cond = Conductor(
        name=branch.name,
        start=(sx, sy, sz),
        end=(ex, ey, ez),
        start_electrode=start,
        end_electrode=end,
        conductor_type=p.conductor_type,
        wire_radius=p.wire_radius_m,
        cross_section=p.cross_section,
        discretize_segment_length=p.segment_length_m,
        coupling_to_soil=p.coupling_to_soil,
        inductance_model=p.inductance_model,
    )
    world.add_conductor(cond)
    return cond

    def site_anchor_point(site: PlannedSite) -> Optional[tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """Connection point in m of the anchor electrode of ``site``.

    The site is materialised into a scratch world, so the point is exactly
    the one a branch without a contact attaches to (``None`` for a site
    without present electrodes). For a rectangular foundation it is a
    corner — the start of its local :math:`-y` side (meshes since audit
    A2G-04, rectangles without cross-braces since user decision Q38) — and
    for a building outline its first vertex, for a circular ring its
    :math:`+x` point, for a strip its start, for a rod its head. The
    generators connect their cables to a site with a horizontal electrode (a
    foundation, a ring, a strip) at the point of those electrodes nearest to
    each cable instead (:func:`site_contact_wires`, user decisions Q41,
    Q43); this point stays the end of everything attached to the site by
    name, and of the generators' conductors at a site with rods only.

    Parameters
    ----------
    site
        A planned site.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of float or None
        ``(x, y, z)`` in m of the anchor electrode's connection point, or
        ``None`` for a site without present electrodes.
    """
    if site.anchor is None:
        return None
    scratch = create_world(soil=HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
    anchor = materialise_site(scratch, site)
    return tuple(float(v) for v in _node_point(scratch, anchor))  # type: ignore[return-value]

    def clean_polygon(
    polygon_xy: "tuple[tuple[float, float], ...] | list[tuple[float, float]]",
    *,
    min_edge_m: float = MIN_POLYGON_EDGE_M,
) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """Drop duplicate and sub-``min_edge_m`` vertices from a closed ring.

    Walks the ring once and keeps a vertex only when it is at least
    ``min_edge_m`` away from the last kept one; finally drops trailing
    vertices whose closing edge (last → first) would be too short. An
    explicitly repeated closing vertex is removed first.

    Parameters
    ----------
    polygon_xy
        Ring vertices ``(x, y)`` in m.
    min_edge_m
        Shortest edge in m that is kept.

    Returns
    -------
    list of tuple
        The cleaned, open ring.
    """
    pts = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in polygon_xy]
    if len(pts) > 1 and math.dist(pts[0], pts[-1]) < 1e-9:
        pts = pts[:-1]
    kept: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
    for p in pts:
        if not kept or math.dist(kept[-1], p) >= min_edge_m:
            kept.append(p)
    while len(kept) >= 3 and math.dist(kept[-1], kept[0]) < min_edge_m:
        kept.pop()
    return kept

    def concrete_shell(
    spec: FoundationElectrodeSpec, *, encased_length_m: float
) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    r"""Effective radius, lumped resistance and coefficient of a shell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spec
        Resolved foundation spec (concrete values only).
    encased_length_m
        Total length :math:`L` in m of the encased wire: every wire of the
        foundation — the perimeter of a ring or of a building outline,
        the perimeter plus the cross-braces of a mesh (user decision Q20).

    Returns
    -------
    effective_radius_m : float
        :math:`r_b = r_a + t` in m when a shell is configured, else the
        bare wire radius :math:`r_a`.
    shell_total_ohm : float
        :math:`R_\text{shell} = C / L` in Ω (0 without shell): the shell
        resistance of the whole foundation under a uniform leakage
        current, equal to the per-wire shells :math:`C / L_j` in
        parallel. Informational; the solver sees the coefficient.
    shell_coefficient_ohm_m : float
        :math:`C = \rho_c/(2\pi)\,\ln(r_b/r_a)` in Ω·m (0 without shell),
        :func:`~groundfield.geometry.electrodes.concrete_shell_coefficient`.

    Notes
    -----
    New in 2026.11. Before the user decision Q20 the development line kept
    the braces of a mesh bare and took the perimeter as the length (keyword
    ``perimeter_m``); 0.15.0 had no such function (its private
    ``grounding._maybe_concrete_shell`` divided by the perimeter).
    """
    if spec.concrete_rho_ohm_m is None:
        return float(spec.wire_radius_m), 0.0, 0.0
    rho_c = float(spec.concrete_rho_ohm_m)
    t = float(spec.concrete_thickness_m)
    if rho_c <= 0.0 or t <= 0.0:
        return float(spec.wire_radius_m), 0.0, 0.0
    r_a = float(spec.wire_radius_m)
    coefficient = concrete_shell_coefficient(rho_c, r_a, t)
    length = float(encased_length_m)
    r_shell = coefficient / length if length > 0.0 else 0.0
    return r_a + t, float(r_shell), float(coefficient)

    MIN_POLYGON_EDGE_M module-attribute ¶

    MIN_POLYGON_EDGE_M = 0.5

    Shortest polygon edge (m) kept in a foundation along a building outline.

    Shorter edges are merged away: a segment shorter than the (concrete-inflated) wire radius would trip the solver's thin-wire guard, and OSM footprints routinely carry centimetre-scale edges without physical meaning for the strip foundation.

    def footprint_mask_key(footprint: BuildingFootprint) -> object:
    """Key of a footprint in :meth:`LvNetworkLayout.foundation_mask`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    footprint
        The building footprint.

    Returns
    -------
    int or str
        ``footprint.osm_id`` when set; otherwise ``"outline:"`` followed
        by the exterior-ring vertices in millimetres, starting at the
        lexicographically smallest vertex. The outline key depends only
        on the geometry, never on the position of the footprint in a
        list or on the Python hash seed.
    """
    if footprint.osm_id is not None:
        return footprint.osm_id
    pts = [
        (int(round(x * 1000.0)), int(round(y * 1000.0)))
        for x, y in footprint.polygon_xy_m
    ]
    start = pts.index(min(pts))
    pts = pts[start:] + pts[:start]
    return "outline:" + ";".join(f"{x},{y}" for x, y in pts)

    Plan vocabulary and constants¶

    The literal types of the plan records and the geometric limits the generators apply.

    SiteRole module-attribute ¶

    SiteRole = Literal['substation', 'cabinet', 'building', 'auxiliary', 'probe']

    Role of a PlannedSite in the network.

    • "substation" — the secondary substation (Ortsnetzstation).
    • "cabinet" — a cable distribution cabinet.
    • "building" — a building of the network (a house or a commercial building).
    • "auxiliary" — the current return electrode of a measurement.
    • "probe" — the voltage probe electrode of a measurement.

    BranchRole module-attribute ¶

    BranchRole = Literal['pen', 'service_drop', 'measurement_lead']

    Role of a PlannedBranch in the network.

    • "pen" — a section of a PEN cable.
    • "service_drop" — the connection of a building to its cable.
    • "measurement_lead" — a metallic lead of a measurement set-up.

    CabinetRule module-attribute ¶

    CabinetRule = Literal['centroid_ray', 'far_end_ray']

    Rule that placed the cable cabinet of a building group (PlannedSite.cabinet_rule, audit W1R2-02).

    • "centroid_ray" — on the ray from the substation through the group's centroid.
    • "far_end_ray" — on the ray through the group's far-end building, because on the centroid ray the cabinet would have stood farther than CabinetConfig.max_far_end_gap_m from its group.

    FoundationOutline module-attribute ¶

    FoundationOutline = Literal['spec', 'ombr', 'polygon']

    How a building footprint shapes a foundation electrode.

    • "ombr" — oriented minimum bounding rectangle of the outline (size, orientation and centre).
    • "polygon" — the outline itself (closed ring; style="ring" foundations only).
    • "spec" — ignore the footprint; keep the spec geometry.

    MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M module-attribute ¶

    MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M = 1.0

    Shortest side (m) of a foundation rectangle taken from a footprint's OMBR.

    A narrower outline — a mapped wall or fence, e.g. 10 m x 5 mm — is widened to this side with a UserWarning; as a 5 mm wide mesh it could not even be built (the mesh span is shorter than the wire radius, audit L5). The AP1 pipeline applied the same 1 m floor to its OMBR foundations.

    SURFACE_LEAD_HEIGHT_M module-attribute ¶

    SURFACE_LEAD_HEIGHT_M = 0.1

    Distance in m of a lead "on the surface" (depth_m = 0) from the ground plane.

    A wire exactly in the soil-surface plane is singular for the image kernels (source and image coincide), and the Sommerfeld earth-return kernel degrades for \(|z|\) below about ten wire radii. 0.1 m keeps a 5 mm lead clear of both; the earth-return impedance of a surface lead is insensitive to the exact height while it is small against the skin depth (hundreds of metres below 1 kHz).

    def lead_axis_z(depth_m: float, coupling_to_soil: str = "isolated") -> float:
    """:math:`z` coordinate in m of a measurement lead's axis.

    Parameters
    ----------
    depth_m
        Configured depth in m: positive into the soil, negative above
        ground, ``0`` on the surface.
    coupling_to_soil
        ``"isolated"`` or ``"galvanic"``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        ``depth_m``; for ``depth_m == 0`` the lead lies
        :data:`SURFACE_LEAD_HEIGHT_M` above the ground (isolated) or
        below it (galvanic: the bare wire touches the soil).
    """
    if depth_m != 0.0:
        return float(depth_m)
    if coupling_to_soil == "galvanic":
        return SURFACE_LEAD_HEIGHT_M
    return -SURFACE_LEAD_HEIGHT_M
